script.title: Porter's Five Forces Model
script.caption_hook: Why is one industry so profitable and another barely survives?

lines.say: Why do some industries earn huge profits and others barely survive?
Five forces shape how profitable an industry can be. That's Porter's Five Forces.
Think of your shop. Newcomers want to open, suppliers sell to you, buyers bargain, substitutes pull customers.
And the rival shops around you?
Rivalry among existing competitors is the fifth force. Many equal rivals and little difference make it strong.
Wait, so a rival coffee brand is a substitute?
No. A rival coffee brand is rivalry. Tea for coffee is a substitute, from another industry.
Oh! Same industry is rivalry, other industry is substitute.
So when is a force strong?
A force is strong when entry is easy, suppliers are few, big buyers switch easily, or rivals are equal.
And what do strong forces do?
Lower industry profit. Weak forces mean higher profit.
So I read the case, find who's pressing, and name that force!
Exactly. Find who presses on profit, then name that force.

Checker: Line 11: the voice line and the board don't match. The voice says 'big buyers switch easily', but the board says only 'Few big buyers'. Make them say the same thing, for example: 'Few, large buyers with low switching costs' (buyer power is high when buyers are concentrated or large and switching costs are low).

Checker: Line 4 board: 'New entrants' should be 'Threat of new entrants' so it matches Porter's label. The lines 'Power of suppliers' and 'Power of buyers' should be 'Bargaining power of suppliers' and 'Bargaining power of buyers', the exact force names students are expected to write.

Checker: Line 11: the voice says 'A force is strong when ...' and then lists conditions for only four forces. It leaves out substitutes, so the list looks complete when it isn't. Either add 'close substitutes are available at a good price-performance' or say 'For example, forces are strong when ...'.
